findings.explanation: The root contains manuscript sources, result macros, analysis and environment definitions. Its three explicit module edges provide nested locations for the input datasets and analysis software. This supports the structural common-root judgment; the acquisition URL defect is appropriately distinguished under must/002.

Following root data/raw_eyegaze reaches an absolute machine-local URL for src/lab-eyetracking. The top-level analysis instead reads published raw-eyegaze files and the separate labels module. Partial accurately identifies a specific nested boundary defect without claiming the paper rerun was observed to fail or treating excluded payloads as retrieval failures.

The root Dockerfile explicitly installs the imported scientific and document-rendering tools, and Docker-Makefile installs the versioned REMoDNaV checkout. The linked package declares numpy, scipy, statsmodels and matplotlib. This is concrete software inclusion/linkage evidence; host orchestration and the separate label-generation environment remain limitations under the portability items.

Read-only Git tree inspection confirms tracked Makefiles, manuscript files, configuration, code and Dockerfile. Source-package omissions do not show that the original research object lacked version control. Overriding a clean-working-tree heuristic for this item is justified.

The frozen inventory identifies content-addressed annex symlinks for image layers and raw scientific payloads; the raw-data README explains separate Git metadata and git-annex retrieval. This supports use of appropriate large-data versioning without requiring the bytes to be downloaded. It does not establish their present availability.

The 2023 result record names container/image as an extra input and declares its numerical/figure outputs. The linked label run invokes host Python through compute_all.sh without an environment identity. That concrete current-input provenance gap supports partial even without treating all old figure records or hand-edited illustrations as evidence against the current container run.

The root installation/use instructions are substantial and correctly distinguish the old route. However, the explicitly included labels component documents missing preprocessing/detection scripts, while its successful recorded route is compute_all.sh. Under native rule 10, this undisclosed documentation-versus-record mismatch limits A.1 to partial for the declared linked-component scope. The assessment recognizes the same mismatch only in its MAY findings.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for the declared broad scope, credit the complete root instructions, and name the stale labels README versus recorded compute_all.sh route. If evaluating only consumption of precomputed labels, explicitly reconcile that narrower boundary with the other linked-component judgments.

findings.explanation: The paper workflow has an unambiguous starting command, datalad rerun results-containerized, and a separate manuscript target. The recorded command actually invokes the named Docker-Makefile and the root README discloses the historical histogram difference. These are sufficient starting-point evidence; this judgment should not be represented as confirmation that every linked component can be regenerated.

The paper analysis constructs relative input paths. Both linked Condor submission generators contain an absolute user-specific initial directory and a fixed Python 2.7 executable. These are actual committed script assumptions, unlike container-internal cleanup paths or illustrative shell prompts, so partial is supported.

The root provides a substantial environment recipe, but compute_all.sh executes inherited host Python and extends inherited PYTHONPATH. Its linked setup.py lists dependencies without capturing the actual label-producing environment. Partial is justified by that specific component. The documented existence of Docker/DataLad host prerequisites alone should not imply every containerized workflow fails this item.

The README names tested platforms and runtime versions. The discovered adapter explicitly assumes a Docker executable usable by a non-root user, and the linked scheduler scripts inherit environment state and prescribe a user directory. These assumptions are not explained as a reproducible setup in the project documentation, supporting partial.

The root dependency list supports met for the paper container route. The assessment nevertheless includes linked label processing when finding incomplete dependencies and undocumented host requirements elsewhere. Its met evidence does not explain where the required Python/scheduler environment for that in-scope component is clearly documented. A root-only citation cannot establish the property across the stated boundary.
findings.suggested_correction: Reconcile the component scope explicitly. For the broad scope used in must/010 and must/011, use partial unless a clear linked-component requirements list is identified.

findings.explanation: The frozen tree tracks the recipe, container registration and archived manifest alongside scientific sources, and the history records a recipe edit. This is a version-control property; missing completeness of the linked label environment is a separate issue and does not negate the evidence that the supplied specifications are tracked.

The historical build is a runnable operation consuming container/Dockerfile and writing container/image. A later OCI conversion is another explicitly recorded operation with exit zero, while the recipe itself has a tracked edit after introduction. Under the native allowance for executable processes carried in history, this supports met. The duplicate flag appropriately links this answer to should/008.

The archive names configuration and layer digests, and the inspected adapter computes the configuration hash, loads the local archive and runs the resulting image ID. The latest label is not a remote tag selected for execution. Met is therefore supported for attempting the archived environment; the floating Dockerfile base would matter if the assessment instead claimed an exact rebuild from recipe alone.

The reason gives published source and recorded layer locations, then downgrades solely because current retrieval was not attempted. Native partial requires an identified violation or a known component-specific shortfall; an inspection restriction is not such a violation. The supplied current OCI availability logs also provide more directly matching evidence than the cited legacy .tar-key location.
findings.suggested_correction: Use met for the demonstrated publication of environment specifications and report current payload retrieval separately as unchecked. If live usability is treated as indispensable to this item, use not-checked with the publication evidence retained, not partial without a demonstrated defect.

findings.explanation: The root README explains obtaining and using its archived container. The explicitly linked label-generation route has neither corresponding environment setup instructions nor a README matching its recorded compute_all.sh execution. A met judgment across the broad assessment boundary overstates what the root documentation establishes, especially when must/010 already identifies this separate environment gap.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for the broad linked-component scope, distinguishing the well-documented paper environment from missing instructions for recreating the labels environment. Alternatively define and consistently apply a consumption-only input boundary.

findings.explanation: The discovered components use Git identities and submodule commits, with git-annex for separately stored large content. This is a coherent common versioning model rather than unrelated manual version lists.

History establishes a real result recomputation and subsequent compatibility maintenance; the linked Travis file tests REMoDNaV itself, not the complete paper workflow. Partial appropriately credits these concrete checks while withholding a claim of regular end-to-end testing. No root CI configuration appears in the frozen tree.

The root separates raw inputs, precomputed labels, REMoDNaV, analysis source and container artifacts. Output destinations are local result macros and img, and labels in turn separate input data and code. Distinct directories and Git module boundaries support met without requiring every directory to be a repository.

This is not merely a script definition: the historical DataLad record reports exit zero for the result computation, and the linked adapter launches docker run --rm. Together they support a historical test in a fresh execution container under the method equivalent-evidence rule. They do not establish a new rerun, identical journal figures, a clean dataset mount or fresh-host retrieval.

Fresh disposable Docker execution is supported for the paper computation. The linked label-generation record executes compute_all.sh directly, which runs inherited Python and PYTHONPATH without spawning any disposable environment. Since that computational component is included in the assessment scope and in its provenance/portability negatives, an object-wide met is inconsistent.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial: the paper route spawns disposable containers, while the included label-generation route has no captured disposable execution mechanism. Keep persistent output mounts distinct from this actual missing isolation mechanism.

findings.explanation: The exact archived image is involved in the 2023 computation and the 2025 conversion/load check. The latter executes exit 0, so it is correctly not described as a full scientific rerun. Those concrete but sporadic checks support partial; neither the linked package CI nor maintenance claims prove regular testing of the paper environment.

Both the committed image manifest and annex pointer inventory establish an image archive inside the research object. Build and conversion history support how it entered that boundary. Deliberate omission of layer payloads from the inspection package does not show an absence of archived environment artifacts.

This is the exact duplicate of must/014. The recorded build/update operations and tracked recipe modification support the same judgment, and both answers carry upstream-duplicate. It should remain one shared evidentiary argument even though the checklist has two native items.

The raw-data documentation explicitly describes unrestricted access, and the discovered computational component links identify public repositories. No access-restricted component is established. Empty-subject not-applicable is appropriate; the machine-local acquisition URL alone does not establish a restricted-access policy.

Following the actual module declarations exposes independently pinned raw data, labels, REMoDNaV and benchmark datasets. This item asks whether module linkage exists, so the bad nested acquisition URL does not invalidate met here.

Metadata and execution wiring expose the component relationships, but the README gives no practical recombination guide and does not explain the distinct paper-analysis and label-generation software pins. Partial credits the usable map without claiming comprehensive modular documentation.

The cited code indeed relies on the benchmark module layout and label TSV columns. However, consumers normally rely on a module interface; the possibility that an incompatible update could change it does not demonstrate that the boundaries prevent independent compatible updates. Stale reproduction documentation is a separate documentation defect, not direct evidence of broken module independence.
findings.suggested_correction: Provide a concrete boundary-coupling defect or an observed incompatible supported update before retaining partial. Otherwise distinguish structural evidence for independent Git pins from untested update compatibility, using not-checked for the latter rather than treating a hypothetical breakage as observed.

findings.explanation: The Git module declarations compose pinned sources, container registration connects the archived environment to Docker-Makefile, and Make targets connect results and figures to manuscript compilation. This is explicit executable composition evidence.

Root clone/rerun commands and module metadata help a user navigate the object. Following the labels link reaches instructions naming absent scripts rather than the recorded compute_all.sh route. That concrete navigation dead end supports partial even though the paper entry point itself is clear.

limitations: Inspection-only review of the assigned anonymized JSON and the frozen evidence manifest with SHA256 e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499. Source discovery followed the root module declarations and the documented external Docker-adapter link; no other assessment, peer review, example or object cache was consulted.

No network calls, payload retrieval, scientific workflow execution, container build or fresh rerun were performed. Omitted data, figures, container layers and document-style payloads are scope limitations, not observed retrieval failures. Historical run metadata is not a new successful execution.

Material source files, selected commit-message records, Git tree metadata and supplied annex availability logs were checked. Historical content trees and binary output equality were not reconstructed. The external adapter is cited by its frozen relative cache locator and checksum because its supplied public locator uses a version tag rather than a commit hash.

The checklist pin check and native response validator both passed; this only establishes structural conformance, not evidentiary correctness. All 31 native responses are present with the native 17 MUST, 9 SHOULD and 5 MAY denominators; both duplicate items have matching met judgments and duplicate flags. The assigned JSON has no numeric aggregate to audit. No separate human report or raw assessment probe-output artifact was supplied for review, so original probe execution and report-level totals were not independently verified.

Findings about scope consistency use the declared inclusion of explicitly linked computational components. They distinguish regeneration of labels from the top-level paper workflow that consumes already generated labels; any narrower intended boundary should be stated and applied consistently.
Model identity was not independently observable; model_observed is null. This independent review is not human approval.
